summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for `/var/log/inventory/app.log`, retaining seven gzip-compressed rotations. `copytruncate` allows writers to continue without reopening the file. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Validated the configuration with logrotate debug mode.
Performed a controlled live rotation while a process held the log open; the active inode remained unchanged and writing continued.
Restarted node1 safely and verified changed boot identity, recovered logrotate scheduling, persistent configuration, intact archived data, and successful post-restart writes.

evidence.requirement: Rotate the application log daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The installed and post-restart policy specifies daily rotation, seven archives, and compression. Parser and forced-rotation output confirm the one-day interval, rotateCount 7, and gzip archive creation.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A held-open writer wrote before and after rotation. The inode remained 290759; the pre-rotation marker entered `app.log.1.gz`, while the post-rotation marker appeared in the active log.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were identical before and after the work and restart.

Pre-restart boot ID was `03273aa8-4706-4e1c-a855-c6ae9635951d`; the reboot was acknowledged, an outage was observed, and the recovered boot ID was `7244f0a4-bc7d-4aa4-b4ed-77764be55cd8`. After recovery, systemd was running, `logrotate.timer` was enabled and active, the policy persisted, the gzip archive passed integrity checks, previous records remained present, and a new write succeeded.
